summary.headline: Orders jumped 13.4% to 789, a strong week, but revenue stayed behind target at 89.6% and cancellations rose sharply to 19.0%.

points.what: Weekly orders reached 789, up 13.4% week on week and 58.1% year on year, above the 8-week average of 707.
points.so_what: This was a good week for volume, though 58.1% year-on-year growth is still below the 75% growth the targets assume.

points.what: Gross revenue was $53,365, up 7.5% week on week and 49.0% year on year, against a weekly target of $59,585.
points.so_what: Revenue came in 89.6% of target, so a strong order week did not close the gap to the weekly target.

points.what: The order cancellation rate rose 4.2 pp to 19.0%, and is 5.4 pp above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $659 of weekly revenue, which weighs on revenue despite the order growth.

points.what: New customer signups rose 28.7% week on week to 287.
points.so_what: Customer acquisition grew faster than orders this week, which grew 13.4%.

points.what: The cancellation rate of 19.0% is flagged as notable, with a 4.2 pp weekly rise against a 1.0 pp threshold.
points.so_what: At roughly $659 of revenue per percentage point, this is the main drag on converting order growth into revenue.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $415,309 against a target of $473,740, a shortfall of $58,431 with 5 weeks left in 2026-Q1.
points.so_what: Reaching the full-quarter target of $774,555 requires $359,246 over the remaining 5 weeks.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate is flagged for maturity and is reported for the week of 02 Feb 2026, with the two most recent weeks not yet mature.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be read yet, so 10.8% describes the week of 02 Feb 2026 only.

points.what: Orders hit 98.4% of the weekly target of 802 (a gap of 13 orders) and revenue 89.6% of the $59,585 target (a gap of $6,220).
points.so_what: Both measures are behind target, and next week's bar is higher for orders at 807 and lower for revenue at $57,620.

points.what: Quarter-to-date and year-to-date revenue both stand at 87.7% of target, $58,431 behind, with Jan and Feb month-to-date both behind.
points.so_what: The quarter and the year are behind target, so this week's growth has not changed the cumulative position.

points.what: Hitting the $3,888,802 full-year target needs $77,189 of revenue per week across the remaining 45 weeks, versus a recent 8-week run-rate of $51,914.
points.so_what: The required pace is well above the current run-rate, so the full-year target is a stretch at this pace.

points.what: EMEA was the largest regional contributor, adding 35 of the 93 extra orders, or 37.6% of the weekly change, on 27.1% growth to 164 orders.
points.so_what: The week's order gain was led by a region holding a 20.8% share, rather than by the largest region.

points.what: LATAM added 26 orders (28.0% of the change, up 32.1%), while APAC added 19 and North America 13 despite their larger shares.
points.so_what: Growth was broad across regions, with all four up year on year, though none of the gains lifted revenue to target.

points.what: Search contributed 42 orders, 45.2% of the weekly change, rising 8.3% to 549 orders and 69.6% of the total; Email fell 2.9% to 34 orders.
points.so_what: The order increase depends mainly on Search, with Organic (+24) and Facebook (+23) adding most of the rest.

points.what: Average order value was $83.51, down 0.2% week on week but up 0.5% against the same week last year.
points.so_what: Order value is essentially flat, so revenue movement is driven by order volume and cancellations rather than basket size.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose to 19.0% from 14.8%, and is 5.4 pp higher than the 13.6% of the same week last year.
points.so_what: This is assessed as bad on both comparisons and reduces the revenue captured from the 789 orders placed.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 02 Feb 2026 was 10.8%, down 0.8 pp from the prior week but 2.9 pp above last year.
points.so_what: Return behaviour improved week on week but remains worse than a year ago, on orders placed in the week of 02 Feb 2026.

points.what: New customer signups were 287, up 28.7% week on week and 5.1% year on year.
points.so_what: Signup growth over the year, at 5.1%, is far below order growth of 58.1%, so volume is leaning on existing customers.

anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
